messages:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: embedding-api high error rate and latency spike detected (rule=embed_tail_latency). Paging oncall.

ivan: i see huge spikes to /v1/embeddings/bulk from 3 IP ranges, 5xxs up and p50->p99 tail rising.

jamie (oncall): on it. i'm pulling traces and checking WAF logs. are we seeing auth failures or just volume?

ivan: mostly 200s for auth but lots of timeouts downstream and some 429s. looks like huge fanout of small batches hitting redis cache causing eviction storms.

lucy (support): getting customer reports about slow embeddings in prod, one customer says timeouts for batch jobs. affected: 2 enterprise orgs (E-42, E-77) doing nightly indexing.

opsbot: WAF: blocked 12k requests in last 10m from suspicious UA patterns, rule 9204 triggered (rapid-bulk-requests).

jamie (oncall): ok quick mitigation plan: 1) enable stricter WAF rule (deny by signature+geo) 2) apply temporary global embed QPS cap 3) disable non-critical bulk endpoint if needed 4) notify customers and start mitigation timeline. agree?

ivan: agree. pushing WAF change now. adding rule: deny if UA contains "ScrapeBot" AND requests/min > 1000.

ivan: applied WAF config (edge): rule id 9204 -> action=block. propagation expected ~30s.

opsbot: WAF: rule 9204 applied across edges in 18s. Estimated drop in malicious traffic: ~78%.

jamie (oncall): nice. i'm adding a global QPS cap for embeddings: 250 QPS global, per-key burst 50. pushing to rate-limiter service.

ivan: rate-limiter policy pushed. snippet:```json
{
  "route": "/v1/embeddings",
  "global_qps": 250,
  "per_key_burst": 50,
  "enforcement": "throttle"
}```

opsbot: rate-limiter: policy accepted by control plane, enforcement active in 12s.

lucy (support): can we craft a short customer message? two orgs already hit us. they need ETA for resolution.

jamie (oncall): quick note: "We're investigating elevated embedding latencies caused by abusive traffic. We've applied stricter edge rules and temporary throughput caps; you may see rate-limited batch jobs. We're prioritizing restoration for affected orgs and will follow up in 30m." send to E-42 & E-77 with postmortem promise.

lucy (support): sent to both customers, asked for logs and whether they can move large background jobs to off-peak window. acked.

ivan: still seeing some tail latencies, looks like internal redis cluster is under pressure. starting a short redis failover to rebalance slots.

opsbot: deploy-bot: rolling restart of embedding-worker pool not started automatically. need approval.

jamie (oncall): approve restart of worker pool (graceful, 1/10 at a time). do it.

ivan: starting rolling restart now. command:```bash
kubectl rollout restart deployment/embed-workers -n inference --time-limit=300s
```

ivan: restart progressing, 3/10 completed, monitoring KV cache miss rate.

opsbot: telemetry: p95 latency dropping from 4200ms -> 900ms after first 6 pods restarted.

jamie (oncall): good sign. keep the QPS cap for 1h, then reevaluate. also add temporary disable for /v1/embeddings/bulk (non-urgent) if traffic doesn't stabilize.

ivan: disabling bulk endpoint flagged as feature-flag toggle: ff_embed_bulk=false. toggled off in control plane.

opsbot: feature flag updated, traffic to /v1/embeddings/bulk dropped to zero. overall ingestion now within limits.

lucy (support): customers responded: E-42 moved nightly indexing to off-peak and saw jobs complete. E-77 asked for rate limit headers to be included in responses (we have X-RateLimit-* now).

jamie (oncall): good. next steps: 1) keep caps for 1h 2) follow-up postmortem + root cause: suspected coordinated scraper using legit API keys (credential stuffing-ish) or stolen tokens. 3) rotate any keys confirmed compromised. 4) prepare WAF signature refinement to avoid false positives.

ivan: collecting logs for 1h window and starting token anomaly scan (per-key QPS abnormality). will surface suspects to security.

opsbot: incident note created: INC-2109-embed-burst. severity: high. initial mitigation: WAF block, global QPS cap, disable bulk endpoint, rolling worker restart.

jamie (oncall): handing off to sandeep for next shift. sandeep pls take over and monitor for 2h, escalate to sec if stolen tokens found.

sandeep: taking it. thanks. i'll pick up logs, token rotation, and follow-up comms.

lucy (support): i'll keep customers updated and draft postmortem template.

jamie (oncall): thanks team. will log timeline and close this thread when stable. :white_check_mark:
